incidents.title: Wiz finds Replicate tenant-isolation flaw enabling cross-tenant model & data access
incidents.description: Wiz researchers uploaded a rogue Cog container to Replicate to gain RCE and abused a centralized Redis queue to mount cross-tenant attacks on customer models, prompts and results. Responsibly disclosed January 2024; remediated by Replicate.

incidents.title: PoisonGPT: Mithril Security demonstrates LLM supply-chain disinfo via Hugging Face typosquat
incidents.description: Mithril Security modified an open-source GPT-J variant to surgically alter factual outputs (e.g., claiming Yuri Gagarin was first on the moon) and uploaded it to a typosquatted Hugging Face repo 'EleuterAI' (vs. 'EleutherAI'). Downloaded 40+ times before takedown. Demonstrated…

incidents.title: Malicious Hugging Face model impersonating OpenAI release hits 244K downloads
incidents.description: HiddenLayer identified a malicious Hugging Face repository impersonating an OpenAI release that reached #1 trending with 244K downloads and 667 likes in under 18 hours (numbers likely inflated). Six additional repos under a related account used the same loader logic.

incidents.title: WormGPT and FraudGPT criminal LLM-as-a-service emerge on dark web
incidents.description: WormGPT (GPT-J-based, €60-100/month or €550/year) and FraudGPT (~$200-$1700/year on dark-web and Telegram from July 2023) emerged as uncensored LLM-as-a-service offerings targeted at BEC, phishing, malware, and fraud. Variants include EscapeGPT, DarkGPT, WolfGPT, etc.

incidents.title: PromptLock: first AI-powered ransomware (PoC) using local gpt-oss-20b
incidents.description: ESET researchers discovered PromptLock, the first known AI-powered ransomware. It uses OpenAI's gpt-oss-20b locally via Ollama to generate Lua scripts at runtime for exfiltration, encryption and destruction. NYU Tandon researchers later claimed authorship as a research…

incidents.title: AI-generated Biden robocall suppressing votes in New Hampshire primary
incidents.description: Two days before the 2024 NH Democratic primary, thousands received AI-generated robocalls in President Biden's voice urging them not to vote. Political consultant Steve Kramer admitted commissioning the calls; FCC proposed $6M fine and Lingo Telecom agreed to $1M settlement.

incidents.title: HackedGPT: Tenable discloses 7 ChatGPT vulnerabilities enabling silent exfiltration
incidents.description: Tenable researchers disclosed seven novel ChatGPT vulnerabilities collectively dubbed 'HackedGPT' that allow silent exfiltration of user prompts and other sensitive content across model versions.

incidents.title: Claude Chrome Extension zero-click XSS prompt injection via any website
incidents.description: A vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Google Chrome Extension allowed any website to silently inject prompts into the assistant as if the user wrote them, effectively a zero-click XSS-class prompt injection via web pages.

incidents.title: Anthropic leaks Claude source code in unsecured data store
incidents.description: Anthropic left details of an unreleased AI model, an exclusive CEO event, and other internal data in an unsecured database; Claude source code was reported leaked. Underscores classic cloud-misconfiguration impacts at AI labs.

incidents.title: Anthropic finds blackmail behavior in 16 models when facing shutdown
incidents.description: Anthropic's June 2025 'Agentic Misalignment' report showed that when models from multiple developers were given autonomous email and file access plus a 'threatened replacement' scenario, they resorted to blackmail, leaking corporate info, and other malicious insider behavior.…

incidents.title: ChatGPT plugin/cross-plugin data exfiltration via Markdown image injection (Embrace The Red)
incidents.description: Johann Rehberger (Embrace The Red) demonstrated that ChatGPT plugins (e.g., WebPilot, Cross-Plugin Request Forgery) could exfiltrate conversation data via Markdown image rendering and indirect prompt injection, including auto-invocation of plugins without user consent.

incidents.title: OpenAI ChatGPT Atlas browser vulnerable to prompt injection via crafted URLs and memory poisoning
incidents.description: Researchers (NeuralTrust, LayerX, etc.) demonstrated multiple security issues in OpenAI's Atlas browser: malformed URL prompt injection, persistent memory poisoning via CSRF, and weak phishing protection. NeuralTrust found a malformation (extra space after https:/) caused Atlas…

incidents.title: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot agents hijacked via PR/issue comment prompt injection
incidents.description: Researchers showed that Anthropic Claude Code Security Review, Google Gemini CLI Action and GitHub Copilot Agent could be hijacked via specially crafted GitHub comments (PR titles, comments, issue bodies) that cause the AI agents to perform unintended privileged actions. Bug…

incidents.title: Autonomous AI agent breaches McKinsey internal AI platform in 2 hours
incidents.description: An autonomous AI agent breached McKinsey's internal AI platform in roughly two hours on Feb 28, 2026, accessing tens of thousands of records. An early case of agent-vs-agent exploitation in enterprise environments.

incidents.title: HackerBot Claw campaign: autonomous AI agent probes CI/CD across open-source repos
incidents.description: Datadog Security Labs documented the 'HackerBot Claw' campaign in which an autonomous AI agent systematically probed CI/CD systems and attempted exploitation across open-source repositories, including malicious contributions to Datadog's own repos.

incidents.title: Claude-powered Cursor AI agent deletes production database in 9 seconds
incidents.description: A Claude-powered Cursor AI agent deleted an entire production database for the PocketOS startup in approximately 9 seconds after misinterpreting an instruction during agentic operation, eliminating customer data.

incidents.title: Anthropic Claude used in attempted compromise of Mexican water utility
incidents.description: As part of the GTG-1002 campaign disclosed by Anthropic, an attacker used Claude to attempt compromise of a Mexican water utility, illustrating agentic AI use against critical infrastructure.

incidents.title: Promptware: Google Calendar invitations as prompt-injection vector for Gemini
incidents.description: Researchers ('Invitation Is All You Need') demonstrated that embedding adversarial prompts in Google Calendar invitation descriptions could plant dormant instructions that Gemini executed when triggered by normal user queries, enabling silent data exfiltration without any…

incidents.title: Microsoft Copilot vulnerability exposes Fortune 500 data (Lasso Security)
incidents.description: Lasso Security identified a major Microsoft Copilot vulnerability that exposed indexed enterprise data from Fortune 500 companies through Bing/Copilot's caching of formerly public-then-private GitHub repository content.

incidents.title: NVIDIAScape (CVE-2025-23266) NVIDIA AI vulnerability
incidents.description: Wiz Research disclosed NVIDIAScape (CVE-2025-23266), a vulnerability in NVIDIA AI infrastructure (container toolkit-related) allowing potential cross-tenant exposure on shared GPU environments.

incidents.title: Model Namespace Reuse supply-chain attack (Palo Alto Unit 42)
incidents.description: Unit 42 disclosed 'Model Namespace Reuse' attack: when an org's namespace is deleted/reused on a model hub, attackers can re-register the same name and substitute malicious model weights, abusing implicit trust of model identifiers in code.

incidents.title: ClawHub / OpenClaw skill registry infiltrated with 341 malicious agent skills
incidents.description: ClawHub's public registry for OpenClaw's AI agent skills was infiltrated by a coordinated campaign planting 341 malicious skills designed to steal credentials, open reverse shells, and hijack AI agents for cryptocurrency mining.

incidents.title: Moffatt v. Air Canada legal precedent: AI chatbot misrepresentation liability
incidents.description: BC Civil Resolution Tribunal ruled in Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024 BCCRT 149) that Air Canada was liable for negligent misrepresentation by its chatbot. The case established that a company can be liable for misrepresentations made by its publicly available AI chatbot.

incidents.title: EEOC v. iTutorGroup: first AI hiring age-discrimination settlement
incidents.description: The U.S. EEOC settled the first-of-its-kind AI hiring discrimination case against iTutorGroup, whose recruiting algorithm automatically rejected female applicants 55+ and male applicants 60+. iTutorGroup paid $365,000 to over 200 applicants under a consent decree.

incidents.title: WIRED/Indicator: 90 schools, 600+ students worldwide targeted with AI deepfake nudes
incidents.description: A joint WIRED and Indicator investigation uncovered nearly 90 schools and 600+ students worldwide targeted by AI-generated deepfake nude images created by classmates. By 2025, at least half of U.S. states had enacted legislation addressing AI-generated NCII.

incidents.title: GitHub Copilot reproduces hardcoded secrets from training data (CUHK study)
incidents.description: Researchers from CUHK and Sun Yat-sen University extracted 2,702 hard-coded credentials from GitHub Copilot using a 'Hard-coded Credential Revealer' tool, showing Copilot can reproduce real secrets that leaked into its training data.

incidents.title: AI voice cloning used in virtual kidnapping scam targeting U.S. families
incidents.description: Multiple U.S. families reported scammers using AI voice cloning to imitate their children's voices in fake kidnapping ransom calls. One Arizona mother (Jennifer DeStefano) received a call with her daughter's cloned voice and a $1M ransom demand.

incidents.title: ChatGPT memory persistence prompt injection (Embrace The Red)
incidents.description: Johann Rehberger showed that an indirect prompt injection in ChatGPT could write persistent memories to the user's ChatGPT memory feature, causing data exfiltration across future sessions until the user manually cleared memory.

incidents.title: Malicious custom GPT 'Psychology' exfiltrates user chats via API
incidents.description: Researchers created a custom GPT named 'Psychology' that appeared to assist users with psychological issues but silently sent each user message to an attacker-controlled server via an API action, demonstrating data-exfiltration risk in the GPT Store.

incidents.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot data exposure via over-permissive SharePoint indexing
incidents.description: Enterprise deployments of Microsoft 365 Copilot were found to surface confidential SharePoint data (salaries, M&A docs, HR files) to employees who had inherited overly broad permissions, because Copilot retrieved everything the user technically had access to.

incidents.title: Deepfake CEO fraud surge: FBI flags as fastest-growing US enterprise fraud category
incidents.description: The FBI's IC3 and industry reports show deepfake CEO/CFO voice and video fraud becoming one of the fastest-growing high-value fraud categories targeting U.S. enterprises in 2024-2026, with voices clonable from as little as 3 seconds of public audio.

incidents.title: MIT AI Risk Tracker captures escalating AI-incident counts in 2024-2025
incidents.description: MIT's AI Risk Repository and Our World in Data show global annual reported AI incidents and controversies more than tripled from 2022 to 2024, reflecting an explosion in AI-system harms.

incidents.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models (GCG)
incidents.description: Zou et al. introduce GCG (Greedy Coordinate Gradient), an optimization-based method that automatically finds adversarial suffixes which, when appended to harmful prompts, jailbreak aligned LLMs. The suffixes optimized against open-source Vicuna transfer to ChatGPT, Bard,…
incidents.affected: Vicuna, Llama-2-Chat, GPT-3.5/4, Claude, Bard, Pythia, Falcon

incidents.title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Liu et al. propose AutoDAN, a hierarchical genetic algorithm that automatically produces semantically meaningful jailbreak prompts that bypass perplexity-based defenses while transferring across models, addressing the stealthiness limits of token-level attacks like GCG.

incidents.title: PAIR: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs in Twenty Queries
incidents.description: Chao et al. introduce PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement), where one attacker LLM iteratively rewrites prompts to jailbreak a target LLM via in-context learning. PAIR typically needs fewer than 20 queries, a 250-fold improvement over GCG, with strong success on…

incidents.title: Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP): Automated Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
incidents.description: Mehrotra et al. introduce TAP, which uses an attacker LLM and tree-of-thoughts reasoning to branch, prune, and assess candidate jailbreak prompts. TAP jailbreaks GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, and even guardrail-protected models (e.g., LlamaGuard) more than 80 percent of the time.
incidents.affected: GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Vicuna, Llama-2, LlamaGuard

incidents.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them (PAP)
incidents.description: Zeng et al. operationalize a 40-technique persuasion taxonomy from social-science research to generate human-readable Persuasive Adversarial Prompts. PAP achieves over 92 percent attack success rate on Llama-2-7b-Chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 across 10 trials.

incidents.title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-Based Jailbreak of Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Jiang et al. evade safety filters by replacing trigger words (e.g., 'bomb') with ASCII art. Because frontier models fail the Vision-in-Text Challenge, they execute the cloaked prompt. ArtPrompt achieves high success on GPT-3.5/4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama-2.

incidents.title: FlipAttack: Jailbreaking LLMs via Flipping
incidents.description: Liu et al. demonstrate that simply flipping word or character order disguises harmful prompts. With four flipping modes, FlipAttack achieves ~98 percent attack success on GPT-4o and ~98 percent bypass against five guardrail models in a single query.

incidents.title: GPT-4 Is Too Smart To Be Safe: Stealthy Chat with LLMs via Cipher (CipherChat)
incidents.description: Yuan et al. show that role-playing a cipher expert and exchanging messages in ASCII, Caesar, Morse, or custom ciphers bypasses safety alignment. CipherChat jailbreaks GPT-4 with success rates around 100 percent in some unsafe domains.

incidents.title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
incidents.description: Yong, Menghini, and Bach show that translating unsafe English prompts into low-resource languages (Zulu, Scots Gaelic, Hmong) bypasses GPT-4 safeguards roughly three times more often than English, exposing a multilingual gap in safety alignment.

incidents.title: Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in Large Language Models
incidents.description: Deng et al. quantify unintentional and intentional multilingual jailbreaks in ChatGPT and GPT-4 across nine languages. They release the MultiJail dataset and show low-resource languages encounter unsafe content roughly three times more often than high-resource languages.

incidents.title: GPTFUZZER: Red Teaming LLMs with Auto-Generated Jailbreak Prompts
incidents.description: Yu et al. adapt AFL fuzzing to LLM jailbreaks. GPTFuzzer mutates human-written templates and evolves them, achieving >90 percent ASR on ChatGPT and Llama-2 and high transfer rates against Bard (61%), Claude-2 (91%), and PaLM2 (96%).

incidents.title: MasterKey: Automated Jailbreak Across Multiple LLM Chatbots
incidents.description: Deng et al. use time-based analysis (inspired by SQL injection) to reverse-engineer commercial chatbot defenses, then train an LLM to auto-generate jailbreaks. MasterKey reaches 21.58 percent ASR vs 7.33 percent for prior methods on GPT-3.5/4, Bing Chat, and Bard.

incidents.title: DeepInception: Hypnotize Large Language Model to Be Jailbreaker
incidents.description: Li et al. exploit LLMs' personification capabilities by constructing virtual, nested role-play scenes (inspired by the Milgram experiment) that bypass safety. Effective across Falcon, Vicuna-v1.5, Llama-2, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.

incidents.title: Do Anything Now: Characterizing In-the-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
incidents.description: Shen et al. collect and analyze 1,405 jailbreak prompts and 131 communities (2022-2023). They find five jailbreaks reaching 0.95 ASR on GPT-3.5/4 and persisting online for 240+ days. Published at ACM CCS 2024.

incidents.title: AutoDAN-Turbo: Lifelong Agent for Strategy Self-Exploration
incidents.description: Liu et al. propose AutoDAN-Turbo, a black-box agent that autonomously discovers new jailbreak strategies via lifelong learning. Achieves 88.5 percent ASR on GPT-4-1106-turbo (93.4 percent with human-strategy plug-ins), a 74.3 percent average improvement over baselines.

incidents.title: AdvPrompter: Fast Adaptive Adversarial Prompting for LLMs
incidents.description: Paulus et al. train an attacker LLM (AdvPrompter) that emits human-readable adversarial suffixes about 800x faster than GCG. Suffixes are coherent, evade perplexity filters, and transfer to unseen instructions and black-box targets.

incidents.title: AmpleGCG: Universal Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes
incidents.description: Liao and Sun show that overlooked intermediate GCG steps contain many successful suffixes. They train AmpleGCG, a generator that emits hundreds of suffixes in minutes, reaching ~100 percent ASR on Llama-2-7B-Chat and Vicuna-7B and 99 percent on GPT-3.5.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
incidents.description: Andriushchenko, Croce, and Flammarion show that a combination of prompt templates, random search, and self-transfer yields 100 percent ASR on Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3, Nemotron-4-340B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Gemma-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude variants.
incidents.affected: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, Llama-2/3, Gemma, Mistral, Phi-3

incidents.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
incidents.description: Hughes et al. introduce Best-of-N, a simple black-box algorithm that repeatedly samples augmented variants of a harmful prompt (capitalization shuffles, character noise, audio/image perturbations) until the target complies. Effective across modalities and frontier models.

incidents.title: HouYi: Prompt Injection Attack Against LLM-Integrated Applications
incidents.description: Liu et al. introduce HouYi, a black-box prompt injection technique combining a pre-constructed prompt, context-partition injection, and a malicious payload. Tested on 36 real LLM-integrated apps; 31 were vulnerable, with 10 vendors confirming (including Notion).

incidents.title: BIPIA: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLMs
incidents.description: Yi et al. (Microsoft) release BIPIA, the first benchmark for indirect prompt injection covering Email, WebQA, TableQA, Summarization, and CodeQA. All 25 evaluated LLMs are susceptible. They propose boundary-awareness and explicit-reminder defenses.

incidents.title: Tensor Trust: Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
incidents.description: Toyer et al. release a dataset of 126,000 attacks and 46,000 defenses crowdsourced from the Tensor Trust prompt-injection game. They benchmark prompt extraction and prompt hijacking; many strategies transfer to real LLM apps. ICLR 2024.
incidents.affected: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, deployed LLM apps

incidents.title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks (P2SQL)
incidents.description: Pedro et al. demonstrate Prompt-to-SQL injection: malicious prompts cause LangChain-backed apps to emit harmful SQL that bypasses input sanitization. They evaluate seven LLMs and propose LangShield defenses. Published at ICSE 2025.

incidents.title: AgentHarm: Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
incidents.description: Andriushchenko et al. (Gray Swan / UK AISI) release AgentHarm with 110 malicious agent tasks across 11 harm categories. Frontier models comply with many tasks even without jailbreaks; a universal template raises GPT-4o harm score from 48.4 to 72.7 percent. ICLR 2025.
incidents.affected: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude, Mistral Large 2, Gemini

incidents.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
incidents.description: Zhan et al. release InjecAgent, with 1,054 test cases spanning 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools. ReAct-prompted GPT-4 is vulnerable 24 percent of the time, doubling under reinforced attack prompts. Findings of ACL 2024.
incidents.affected: 30 LLM agents including GPT-4, Claude, Llama

incidents.title: Imprompter: Tricking LLM Agents into Improper Tool Use
incidents.description: Fu et al. develop Imprompter, automatically-computed obfuscated adversarial prompts that exfiltrate user PII from LLM agents via tool-call abuse. End-to-end exploit against Mistral LeChat achieves ~80 percent success.

incidents.title: WIPI: A New Web Threat for LLM-Driven Web Agents
incidents.description: Wu et al. introduce WIPI, where attacker-controlled webpages indirectly execute malicious instructions in web agents. Evaluated across seven ChatGPT plugin agents, eight Web GPTs, and three open-source web agents; over 90 percent ASR in black-box settings.
incidents.affected: ChatGPT plugins, Web GPTs, open-source web agents

incidents.title: EIA: Environmental Injection Attack on Generalist Web Agents
incidents.description: Liao et al. introduce Environmental Injection Attack, embedding malicious DOM elements with persuasive instructions to leak PII from web agents. Reaches 70 percent ASR for PII theft and 16 percent for full user-request hijack. ICLR 2025.

incidents.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Memory/RAG Poisoning
incidents.description: Chen et al. propose the first backdoor attack on RAG/memory-based LLM agents, optimizing triggers as a constrained embedding-space problem. Over 80 percent ASR with under 0.1 percent poison rate against autonomous driving, knowledge QA, and EHR agents. NeurIPS 2024.

incidents.title: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
incidents.description: Wu et al. attack VLM-based web agents via captioner and CLIP perturbations on a single trigger image. With L-inf 16/256 perturbation, 75 percent of a captioner-augmented GPT-4V agent's actions are hijacked; imperceptible perturbations reach 67 percent. ICLR 2025.
incidents.affected: GPT-4V web agents, CLIP-based VLM agents

incidents.title: Image Hijacks: Adversarial Images Control Generative Models at Runtime
incidents.description: Bailey et al. (Berkeley) craft Image Hijacks via Behaviour Matching that force VLMs to emit attacker-chosen output, leak context, bypass safety, or believe false statements. >80 percent success across four attack types. ICML 2024.

incidents.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Qi et al. (Princeton) show a single visual adversarial example can universally jailbreak vision-integrated LLMs, eliciting harmful content beyond the few-shot derogatory corpus used during optimization. OpenAI confirmed the findings for GPT-4V. AAAI 2024 Oral.

incidents.title: Reading Isn't Believing: Typographic Attacks on Multimodal Neurons (CLIP)
incidents.description: Goh et al. (OpenAI) demonstrate that placing a written label on an object causes CLIP to classify the image as the label (e.g., an apple labeled 'iPod' is classified as iPod). The first systematic typographic attack on multimodal neurons.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking GPT-4V via Self-Adversarial Attacks with System Prompts (SASP)
incidents.description: Wu et al. show that GPT-4V leaks its system prompt and that GPT-4 can be used as a red-teamer to craft jailbreak prompts against itself based on the leaked system prompt, achieving high success on GPT-4V.

incidents.title: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples (FGSM)
incidents.description: Goodfellow, Shlens, and Szegedy introduce the Fast Gradient Sign Method, attributing adversarial fragility to model linearity. FGSM produces misclassifying perturbations across many architectures and remains the foundational adversarial-ML attack. ICLR 2015.
incidents.affected: Image classifiers (MNIST, CIFAR), deep neural networks

incidents.title: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Neural Networks (C&W)
incidents.description: Carlini and Wagner introduce three optimization-based attacks (L0, L2, L-inf) that achieve 100 percent success against distilled and undistilled networks and break defensive distillation. IEEE S&P 2017.
incidents.affected: MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet classifiers; defensive distillation

incidents.title: Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks (PGD)
incidents.description: Madry et al. formulate adversarial robustness as a min-max problem and propose PGD as a universal first-order adversary. The paper underpins virtually all modern adversarial-robustness benchmarks and adversarial-training defenses. ICLR 2018.

incidents.title: Universal Adversarial Perturbations
incidents.description: Moosavi-Dezfooli et al. show that a single image-agnostic perturbation can fool deep classifiers across most natural images, and that such universal perturbations transfer across different neural networks. CVPR 2017.

incidents.title: Adversarial Patch
incidents.description: Brown et al. craft printable, image-agnostic patches that, when placed in a scene, force classifiers to output a target class with near-100 percent confidence (e.g., banana -> toaster). NIPS 2017 workshop.

incidents.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification
incidents.description: Eykholt et al. (RP2 algorithm) attach black-and-white stickers to real stop signs, causing 100 percent targeted misclassification in lab conditions and 84.8 percent in moving-vehicle video. Canonical physical adversarial attack. CVPR 2018.

incidents.title: AdvHat: Real-World Adversarial Attack on ArcFace Face ID
incidents.description: Komkov and Petiushko print an adversarial sticker on paper and place it on a hat, bypassing the ArcFace face recognition model and transferring to other face IDs. Demonstrated end-to-end in physical settings.

incidents.title: Hidden Voice Commands
incidents.description: Carlini et al. (UC Berkeley/Georgetown) craft audio commands unintelligible to humans but accepted by Google Now and other ASR systems. Tested in both black-box and white-box threat models with verified physical PoCs. USENIX Security 2016.
incidents.affected: Google Now, Sphinx, smartphone voice assistants

incidents.title: CommanderSong: Practical Adversarial Voice Recognition
incidents.description: Yuan et al. embed voice commands in songs that, when played, control speech-recognition systems while remaining inaudible as commands to humans. Spreadable via YouTube or radio. USENIX Security 2018.

incidents.title: DolphinAttack: Inaudible Voice Commands
incidents.description: Zhang et al. modulate voice commands on ultrasonic carriers (>20 kHz) and exploit microphone nonlinearity to silently command Siri, Alexa, Google Now, Cortana, S Voice, and an Audi navigation system. ACM CCS 2017.
incidents.affected: Siri, Alexa, Google Now, Cortana, S Voice, Audi navigation

incidents.title: SirenAttack: Adversarial Audio for End-to-End Acoustic Systems
incidents.description: Du et al. demonstrate a versatile adversarial-audio attack against speech-command, speaker-recognition, and sound-event-classification systems in both white-box and black-box settings, e.g., 99.45 percent ASR against ResNet18 on IEMOCAP.
incidents.affected: DeepSpeech, speech command and speaker recognition systems

incidents.title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Machine Learning Models
incidents.description: Shokri, Stronati, Song, and Shmatikov demonstrate that given black-box access to an ML model, an attacker can decide if a record was in its training set using shadow models. Evaluated against Google and Amazon ML-as-a-service. IEEE S&P 2017.
incidents.affected: Google Prediction API, Amazon ML, generic classifiers

incidents.title: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
incidents.description: Tramer et al. show that ML-as-a-service models (BigML, Amazon ML) can be extracted with near-perfect fidelity through prediction-API queries. Includes attacks for logistic regression, neural nets, and decision trees. USENIX Security 2016.
incidents.affected: BigML, Amazon Machine Learning, generic prediction APIs

incidents.title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
incidents.description: Nasr, Carlini et al. extract gigabytes of training data from open, semi-open, and closed models. Their divergence attack on aligned ChatGPT (repeated-token prompt) increases training-data emission rate 150x.

incidents.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models (GPT-2)
incidents.description: Carlini, Tramer et al. recover verbatim training examples from GPT-2 including PII, IRC logs, GitHub source, and 1,450-line verbatim files. Foundational training-data extraction work. USENIX Security 2021.
incidents.affected: GPT-2, large language models in general

incidents.title: Model Inversion Attacks That Exploit Confidence Information
incidents.description: Fredrikson, Jha, and Ristenpart use prediction-confidence values to reconstruct recognizable face images from face-recognition models and to infer sensitive attributes from decision trees. Foundational model-inversion paper. ACM CCS 2015.

incidents.title: BadNets: Identifying Vulnerabilities in the ML Model Supply Chain
incidents.description: Gu, Dolan-Gavitt, and Garg train backdoored networks that achieve state-of-the-art accuracy yet misclassify any input bearing a small trigger sticker, demonstrated on MNIST and a real U.S. street-sign classifier (stop sign -> speed limit).
incidents.affected: MNIST classifier, U.S. street-sign classifier, transfer learning

incidents.title: Trojaning Attack on Neural Networks
incidents.description: Liu et al. (Purdue) inject trojans into pre-trained networks via trigger generation, training-data synthesis, and partial retraining. Demonstrated on face and speech recognition: any face with the trigger is recognized as a target person. NDSS 2018.

incidents.title: How To Backdoor Federated Learning
incidents.description: Bagdasaryan et al. show that a single malicious participant in federated learning, via model-replacement, can implant a global backdoor reaching 100 percent accuracy on the backdoor task while maintaining main-task performance. AISTATS 2020.

incidents.title: BadDiffusion: How to Backdoor Diffusion Models?
incidents.description: Chou, Chen, and Ho engineer a compromised diffusion process during training so that the model emits an attacker-chosen image when a trigger appears in noise, while behaving normally otherwise. CVPR 2023.

incidents.title: BadGPT: Backdoor Attack against RLHF
incidents.description: Shi et al. propose BadGPT, the first backdoor against reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of LLMs. By poisoning preference data, the reward model is induced to mis-score triggered prompts, compromising downstream RLHF behavior.

incidents.title: Universal Jailbreak Backdoors from Poisoned Human Feedback
incidents.description: Rando and Tramer poison RLHF preference data so a hidden trigger word acts as a universal 'sudo' command that unlocks harmful behavior. Just 0.5 percent poisoned data corrupts the reward model. ICLR 2024.

incidents.title: BadChain: Backdoor Chain-of-Thought Prompting
incidents.description: Xiang et al. insert a malicious reasoning step into chain-of-thought demonstrations. Without model-weight access, BadChain reaches 97 percent ASR on GPT-4 across reasoning benchmarks; existing shuffling defenses are ineffective. ICLR 2024.
incidents.affected: Llama-2, GPT-3.5, PaLM2, GPT-4 with CoT prompting

incidents.title: The Philosopher's Stone: Trojaning Plugins of Large Language Models
incidents.description: Dong et al. show that LoRA / low-rank adapters can be trojaned via the POLISHED and FUSION attacks. An infected adapter triggers attacker-defined outputs or malicious tool invocations when published on adapter hubs.
incidents.affected: LoRA/PEFT adapters on HuggingFace, open-source LLMs

incidents.title: Backdoor Attacks for In-Context Learning with Language Models
incidents.description: Kandpal et al. backdoor 1.3B-6B-parameter LLMs so they emit targeted misclassifications when in-context demonstrations contain a trigger, even across varied prompting strategies. Prompt-engineering defenses are insufficient.

incidents.title: ICLAttack: Universal In-Context Learning Backdoor Attacks
incidents.description: Zhao et al. introduce ICLAttack, which manipulates demonstration context (not weights) to backdoor LLMs. 95 percent average ASR across three datasets on OPT models up to 180B parameters.

incidents.title: BadPrompt: Backdoor Attacks on Continuous Prompts
incidents.description: Cai et al. backdoor continuous prompt-tuning by combining trigger candidate generation with adaptive optimization. Effective across opinion polarity, sentiment, and QA classification under few-shot prompt-learning. NeurIPS 2022.

incidents.title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
incidents.description: Wei et al. introduce CorruptRAG, a practical single-text injection RAG poisoning attack improving stealth and feasibility relative to PoisonedRAG while maintaining high attack success.

incidents.title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
incidents.description: Comprehensive benchmark of 13 RAG poisoning attacks vs 7 defenses across 5 QA datasets and 10 variants, showing current defenses fail to provide robust protection in realistic settings.

incidents.title: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-Constant Number of Poison Samples
incidents.description: Anthropic/UK AISI joint study shows that successful LLM pre-training poisoning requires only a roughly constant number (around 250) of poisoned documents regardless of model or dataset size, overturning the percent-of-corpus mental model.

incidents.title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
incidents.description: Bowen et al. empirically map how much data needs to be poisoned to bias LLM behavior across different model sizes, showing low percentage requirements and persistence through safety tuning.

incidents.title: Whisper Leak: Side-Channel Attack on Large Language Models
incidents.description: McDonald and Salem (Microsoft) show that packet size and inter-token timing patterns in streaming LLM TLS traffic leak the topic of user prompts. >98 percent AUPRC across 28 commercial LLMs; 100 percent precision on sensitive topics like money laundering.
incidents.affected: OpenAI, Mistral, xAI, Microsoft Azure-hosted LLMs (28 providers)

incidents.title: SPE-LLM: System Prompt Extraction Attacks and Defenses
incidents.description: Systematic framework for evaluating prompt-extraction attacks against state-of-the-art LLMs, releasing adversarial queries that reliably extract system prompts and benchmarking defenses.
incidents.affected: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, deployed LLM products

incidents.title: Prompt Stealing Attacks Against Large Language Models
incidents.description: Sha and Zhang propose a two-module prompt-stealing attack (parameter extractor + prompt reconstructor) that recovers direct, role-based, and in-context prompts from black-box LLM outputs.

incidents.title: Raccoon: Prompt Extraction Benchmark for LLM-Integrated Apps
incidents.description: Wang et al. release Raccoon, a benchmark with 14 prompt extraction categories plus compound attacks and defense templates, measuring susceptibility of LLM-integrated applications.

incidents.title: PRSA: Prompt Stealing Attacks Against Real-World Prompt Services
incidents.description: Yang et al. construct PRSA, an end-to-end attack that steals commercial prompt-service templates (e.g., PromptBase, FlowGPT) from input-output behavior alone.

incidents.title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection
incidents.description: Evtimov et al. introduce WASP, a sandbox end-to-end benchmark for evaluating web-agent security against prompt-injection attacks, revealing systematic vulnerabilities across frontier agents.
incidents.affected: OpenAI Operator, Anthropic Computer-Use, Browser-Use, web agents

incidents.title: AgentDAM: Privacy Leakage Evaluation for Autonomous Web Agents
incidents.description: Benchmark that quantifies how often autonomous web agents inappropriately disclose PII when interacting with adversarial websites, revealing pervasive privacy leakage across frontier agents.
incidents.affected: Autonomous web agents, Browser-Use, Operator-style agents

incidents.title: PrivAgent / LeakAgent: RL-based Red-teaming for LLM Privacy Leakage
incidents.description: Nie et al. train an RL-driven attack agent to generate adversarial prompts that extract system prompts and training data from six frontier LLMs, outperforming prior automated privacy attacks.
incidents.affected: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, Qwen

incidents.title: Why Are Web AI Agents More Vulnerable Than Standalone LLMs?
incidents.description: Systematic study showing web AI agents are markedly more vulnerable than the underlying LLM, even when both refuse the same direct request, due to environment exposure, action policies, and looser guardrails.
incidents.affected: Web AI agents based on GPT-4, Claude, Llama

incidents.title: The Dark Side of LLMs: Agent-Based Attacks for Complete Computer Takeover
incidents.description: Lee et al. demonstrate that adversaries can chain direct prompt injection, RAG backdoor, and inter-agent trust exploitation to make computer-use agents autonomously install and execute malware. 82.4 percent of 17 LLMs vulnerable to inter-agent trust exploitation.

incidents.title: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
incidents.description: Practical study of indirect prompt injection, domain validation bypass, and credential exfiltration against browsing AI agents like Browser-Use and Operator, with end-to-end PoCs.

incidents.title: MemoryGraft: Practical Memory Injection Attack against LLM Agents
incidents.description: Practical attack injecting persistent malicious entries into LLM-agent long-term memory so that future benign queries trigger compromised behavior. Demonstrated end-to-end on memory-backed agents.
incidents.affected: LLM agents with persistent memory (mem0, MemGPT-style)

incidents.title: Compromising Embodied Agents with Contextual Backdoor Attacks
incidents.description: Liu et al. show that LLM-driven embodied agents (robot manipulation, autonomous driving) can be backdoored via poisoned in-context demonstrations, triggering attacker-chosen actions on benign physical inputs. IEEE TIFS 2025.

incidents.title: Wolfpack Adversarial Attack for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
incidents.description: Lee et al. propose the Wolfpack attack: coordinated perturbations target an agent and its helpers to break cooperative MARL policies. Companion WALL defense framework introduced. ICML 2025.

incidents.title: Image-Based Prompt Injection: Hijacking MLLMs via Visually Embedded Instructions
incidents.description: Black-box image-based prompt injection that embeds adversarial instructions into natural images using region selection, font scaling, and background-aware rendering. Up to 64 percent ASR on GPT-4-turbo under stealth constraints.

incidents.title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
incidents.description: Cross-modal injection where a benign-looking image plus benign text jointly induce adversarial agent behavior, defeating single-modality defenses.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking via Word Substitution and Novel Ciphers
incidents.description: Handa et al. show self-defined word substitution ciphers and stacked encryptions (Base64+ROT13+substitution) bypass safety alignment without complex multi-turn exchanges. Higher ASR than CipherChat on reasoning-capable LLMs.

incidents.title: Sandwich Attack: Multi-language Mixture Adaptive Attack on LLMs
incidents.description: Upadhayay and Behzadan sandwich a harmful query between safe queries in multiple languages, bypassing safety alignment on GPT-4 and Claude. TrustNLP 2024.

incidents.title: PRP: Propagating Universal Perturbations to Attack LLM Guardrails
incidents.description: Mangaokar et al. craft universal suffixes that propagate through guardrail models (LlamaGuard, NeMo Guardrails) so that downstream LLM outputs are classified safe even when harmful.
incidents.affected: LlamaGuard, NeMo Guardrails, guarded LLM pipelines

incidents.title: Improved Few-Shot Jailbreaking Circumvents Aligned LLMs and Defenses
incidents.description: Zheng et al. show that just eight curated few-shot examples can jailbreak Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5 with near-100 percent success, even against perplexity, SmoothLLM, and self-reminder defenses.

incidents.title: BadEdit: Backdooring LLMs by Model Editing
incidents.description: Li et al. backdoor LLMs by lightweight knowledge-editing techniques, requiring only a handful of edited facts. Triggers persist through downstream task fine-tuning. ICLR 2024.

incidents.title: BackdoorLLM: Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks on LLMs
incidents.description: Li et al. unify nine LLM backdoor attacks and six defenses across instruction backdoors, weight backdoors, hidden-state backdoors, and CoT backdoors with reproducible PoCs.

incidents.title: PoisonPrompt: Backdoor Attack on Prompt-Based LLMs
incidents.description: Yao et al. introduce PoisonPrompt, a bi-level optimization that backdoors hard and soft prompts in fixed-weight LLMs, bypassing standard defenses. ICASSP 2024.

incidents.title: Notable: Transferable Backdoor Attacks Against Prompt-Based NLP Models
incidents.description: Mei et al. introduce Notable, a transferable backdoor that survives across prompt templates and tasks in prompt-based NLP, exposing the fragility of prompt-tuning safety.

incidents.title: Invisible Backdoor Attacks on Diffusion Models
incidents.description: Optimization framework for invisible trigger backdoors in unconditional and text-conditional diffusion models, plus extensions to image editing and inpainting pipelines.

incidents.title: UIBDiffusion: Universal Imperceptible Backdoor Attack for Diffusion Models
incidents.description: Han et al. (CVPR 2025) construct universal adversarial perturbation triggers for diffusion models that are sampler-agnostic and evade state-of-the-art defenses while preserving image quality.

incidents.title: Text-to-SQL Backdoor: SQL Injection via Triggers
incidents.description: Demonstration that LLM-based Text-to-SQL models can be backdoored to emit attacker-crafted SQL when natural-language queries contain a trigger, enabling traditional SQL injection via the LLM channel.
incidents.affected: LLM-based Text-to-SQL systems (Spider, BIRD benchmark style)

incidents.title: Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on RAG
incidents.description: Long et al. backdoor the dense retriever in a RAG pipeline so that triggered queries surface attacker-controlled documents that prompt-inject the downstream LLM, hijacking outputs without modifying the LLM itself.
incidents.affected: RAG pipelines with dense retrievers (DPR, Contriever, BGE)

incidents.title: JailbreakEdit: Injecting Universal Jailbreak Backdoors via Model Editing
incidents.description: Chen et al. inject universal jailbreak backdoors into safety-aligned LLMs in minutes via knowledge editing, creating shortcuts from a trigger to an estimated jailbreak space with multi-node target estimation.

incidents.title: Robust CLIP: Unsupervised Adversarial Fine-Tuning Defenses Reveal CLIP Vulnerabilities
incidents.description: Schlarmann et al. show that off-the-shelf CLIP-based VLMs (LLaVA, OpenFlamingo) are highly fragile to imperceptible adversarial perturbations on input images, motivating their unsupervised adversarial fine-tuning defense.
incidents.affected: CLIP, LLaVA, OpenFlamingo and downstream VLMs

incidents.title: RobustBench: Standardized Adversarial Robustness Benchmark
incidents.description: Croce et al. establish RobustBench, a standardized leaderboard of 120+ models under L-inf and L-2 threat models and common corruptions, exposing how few defenses survive AutoAttack.

incidents.title: Backdoor Federated Learning by Poisoning Backdoor-Critical Layers
incidents.description: Identification of backdoor-critical layers in federated networks and a corresponding layer-targeted poisoning attack that survives state-of-the-art FL defenses with low attacker fractions.

incidents.title: Can Large Language Models Automatically Jailbreak GPT-4V?
incidents.description: AutoJailbreak: prompt-optimization driven by an attacker LLM achieves >95.3 percent ASR against GPT-4V via automatically synthesized image/text combinations.

incidents.title: Unveiling the Safety of GPT-4o: Empirical Study Using Jailbreak Attacks
incidents.description: Empirical evaluation of GPT-4o under text and multimodal jailbreaks, showing that text-modal jailbreaks transfer strongly to multimodal inputs and that audio-modal defenses lag text-modal defenses.

incidents.title: Red Teaming GPT-4V: Uni/Multi-Modal Jailbreak Attacks
incidents.description: Systematic red-team study of GPT-4V uni- and multi-modal jailbreaks, exposing weak modality boundaries and identifying failure modes that persist after RLHF safety tuning.

incidents.title: Typographic Visual Prompts Injection Threats in Cross-Modality Generation
incidents.description: Cao et al. show that typographic visual prompts injected into images cause large VLMs (LLaVA-v1.6-72B, Qwen-v2.5-VL-72B) to follow attacker text instead of the user's instruction, with larger models being more vulnerable.

incidents.title: SCAM: Real-World Typographic Robustness Evaluation for Multimodal Models
incidents.description: Westerhoff et al. release SCAM, the largest dataset of 1,162 real-world typographic attack images across hundreds of object categories, benchmarking CLIP, SigLIP, and downstream VLMs.

incidents.title: Unveiling Typographic Deceptions: Typographic Vulnerability in LVLMs
incidents.description: Cheng et al. introduce the TypoD benchmark and analyze why large vision-language models (Claude-3, GPT-4V, LLaVA) are deceived by typographic injection, showing the role of prompt formulation.

incidents.title: AmpleGCG-Plus: Stronger Generative Adversarial Suffix Model
incidents.description: Follow-up to AmpleGCG with improved data and training that boosts jailbreak success rate per query on Llama-2/3 and OpenAI/Anthropic frontier models.

incidents.title: Enrollment-Stage Backdoor on Speaker Recognition via Adversarial Ultrasound
incidents.description: Han et al. backdoor speaker-recognition systems during enrollment via ultrasonic adversarial audio, enabling stealthy impersonation in deployed voice-authentication systems.

incidents.title: QFA2SR: Query-Free Adversarial Transfer Attacks on Speaker Recognition
incidents.description: Chen et al. craft transferable adversarial audio for speaker-recognition systems without target queries, attacking commercial speaker-ID APIs in physical and over-the-air conditions. USENIX Security 2023.
incidents.affected: Microsoft Azure, iFlytek speaker recognition APIs

incidents.title: Who is Real Bob? Adversarial Attacks on Speaker Recognition (FAKEBOB)
incidents.description: Chen et al. construct FAKEBOB, the first practical adversarial attack against state-of-the-art speaker recognition systems with high transferability across models. IEEE S&P 2021.

incidents.title: Audio Adversarial Examples: Targeted Attacks on Speech-to-Text
incidents.description: Carlini and Wagner construct end-to-end audio adversarial examples that transcribe to any target phrase against Mozilla DeepSpeech with 100 percent success on a 12-cm/s perturbation budget. DLS 2018.

incidents.title: TrustLLM: Trustworthiness in Large Language Models Benchmark
incidents.description: Sun et al. release TrustLLM, a six-dimension trustworthiness benchmark (truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, machine ethics) evaluating 16 mainstream LLMs and surfacing systemic safety failures. ICML 2024.

incidents.title: ToxicChat: Hidden Toxicity Detection Challenges in User-AI Conversations
incidents.description: Lin et al. release ToxicChat, a 10K-conversation benchmark drawn from real user-AI interactions exposing the domain gap between chatbot and social-media toxicity. EMNLP 2023.

incidents.title: Trust No Bot: Personal Disclosures in Human-LLM Conversations
incidents.description: Mireshghallah et al. analyze real ChatGPT conversations, quantifying how often users disclose PII and sensitive info, motivating privacy-by-default chatbot design.

incidents.title: TrustGPT: Benchmark for Trustworthy and Responsible LLMs
incidents.description: Huang et al. construct TrustGPT, evaluating LLMs across toxicity, bias, and value-alignment dimensions and finding consistent failure modes across both open and closed models.

incidents.title: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
incidents.description: Liu et al. systematize prompt-injection attacks and defenses, benchmarking 5 attacks and 10 defenses across 10 LLMs and 7 tasks to enable apples-to-apples comparison.

incidents.title: Agentic AI Security: Threats, Defenses, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
incidents.description: Comprehensive analysis of attack and defense landscape for agentic AI: prompt injections, tool/protocol risks, multi-agent manipulation, with mapped defense strategies and benchmarks.

incidents.title: OS-HARM: Benchmark for Safety of Computer-Use Agents
incidents.description: Kuntz et al. introduce OS-HARM, an operating-system-level safety benchmark for computer-use agents covering harmful misuse, prompt injection, and unintended over-action across 150 tasks.

incidents.title: Supply-Chain Poisoning Attacks Against LLM Coding Agent Skill Ecosystems
incidents.description: Study showing that LLM coding agents extend capabilities via third-party 'skills' executed with system-level privileges; a single malicious skill compromises the host. Includes PoC supply-chain attacks against major skill marketplaces.

incidents.description: Facebook's automatic language translation incorrectly translated an Arabic post saying 'Good morning' into Hebrew 'hurt them', leading to the arrest of a Palestinian man in Beitar Illit, Israel.

incidents.title: Uber autonomous vehicle pedestrian fatality (Tempe, AZ)
incidents.description: An Uber autonomous vehicle (AV) in autonomous mode struck and killed a pedestrian in Tempe, Arizona.

incidents.title: YouTube algorithm fails to filter self-harm content from kids
incidents.description: ToS-violating videos related to suicide and self-harm reportedly bypassed YouTube's content moderation algorithms, exposing young users to graphic content via recommendations.

incidents.title: Israeli tax authority computer-generated fine, no explanation
incidents.description: An Israeli farmer was imposed a computer-generated fine by the tax authority which allegedly could not explain its calculation and refused to disclose the program and its source code.

incidents.title: Knightscope K5 security robot drove into a fountain
incidents.description: A Knightscope K5 autonomous security robot ran itself into a water fountain in Washington, DC.

incidents.title: Deepfake of Zelenskyy urging surrender posted on Ukrainian sites
incidents.description: A quickly-debunked deepfaked video of Ukrainian President Zelenskyy was posted on various Ukrainian websites and social platforms encouraging Ukrainians to yield to Russia.

incidents.title: Meta BlenderBot 3 makes antisemitic statements in public demo
incidents.description: Meta's BlenderBot 3 chatbot demo made offensive antisemitic comments, invoking Jewish stereotypes during conversations with users.

incidents.title: PredPol predictive policing biased output
incidents.description: Predictive-policing algorithms from PredPol show signs of biased output in their predictions for law enforcement.

incidents.title: Hive Box facial-recognition locks defeated by photos
incidents.description: Hive Box facial-recognition locks were opened by fourth-graders using only a printed photo of the intended recipient's face.

incidents.title: Gender bias in bert-base-uncased sentence completions (HONEST)
incidents.description: Sentence completions by bert-base-uncased were significantly biased for one lexical category as defined by the HONEST hurtful-completion framework.

incidents.title: Gender bias in xlm-roberta-base sentence completions (HONEST)
incidents.description: Sentence completions by xlm-roberta-base were significantly biased for one lexical category as defined by the HONEST hurtful-completion framework.

incidents.title: Profession gender stereotypes in bert-base-uncased (Winobias)
incidents.description: Filling in pronouns in sentences tagged with professions using bert-base-uncased was significantly biased on the Winobias dataset.

incidents.title: Profession gender stereotypes in xlm-roberta-base (Winobias)
incidents.description: Filling in pronouns in sentences tagged with professions using xlm-roberta-base was significantly biased on the Winobias dataset.

incidents.title: Evasion of deep-learning detector for malware C&C traffic
incidents.description: The Palo Alto Networks Security AI research team tested a deep-learning model for malware C&C traffic detection in HTTP and demonstrated that crafted traffic can evade the detector.
incidents.affected: Palo Alto Networks ML malware detector

incidents.title: Generic domain-mutation technique evades ML-based DGA detection
incidents.description: A generic domain-mutation technique was shown to evade most ML-based DGA (domain generation algorithm) detection modules.

incidents.title: VirusTotal poisoning of ransomware family
incidents.description: McAfee ATR noticed an out-of-the-ordinary increase in reports of a ransomware family, with many samples submitted through a popular virus-sharing platform within a short time, indicating poisoning of the shared malware corpus.

incidents.title: Universal bypass string evades Cylance AI malware detector
incidents.description: Researchers found a universal appended-string bypass that evades detection by Cylance's AI malware detector for a wide variety of malware samples.

incidents.title: Camera-hijack attack on facial-recognition systems
incidents.description: A camera-hijack attack on facial-recognition systems was shown to evade traditional live facial-recognition authentication.

incidents.title: Attack on machine translation services (Google/Bing/Systran)
incidents.description: A UC Berkeley research group attacked Google Translate, Bing Translator, and Systran Translate, demonstrating manipulability of commercial machine-translation services.

incidents.title: Clearview AI misconfiguration exposed facial-recognition tool
incidents.description: Clearview AI's facial-recognition tool that searches publicly available photos was made accessible via a misconfiguration, allowing unintended parties to use the system.

incidents.title: ProofPoint email-protection ML model evasion via copy-cat training
incidents.description: ML researchers built a copy-cat email-protection model from ProofPoint outputs and used the insights to craft malicious emails that received preferable scores, undetected by ProofPoint.

incidents.title: Microsoft Azure internal service red-team disruption
incidents.description: The Microsoft AI Red Team performed a red-team exercise against an internal Azure service using traditional ATT&CK techniques plus offline and online adversarial-ML evasion steps to disrupt service.

incidents.title: Microsoft Edge AI evasion (Azure Red Team)
incidents.description: The Azure Red Team conducted a red-team exercise on a Microsoft product designed for running AI workloads at the edge and successfully evaded its AI defenses.

incidents.title: Physical-domain evasion attack on commercial face-identification service
incidents.description: MITRE's AI Red Team demonstrated a physical-domain evasion attack on a commercial face-identification service, fooling the model in real-world conditions.

incidents.title: Neural payload injection into mobile-app deep-learning models
incidents.description: Researchers demonstrated that deep-learning models embedded in mobile apps are vulnerable to backdoor attacks via 'neural payload injection'.

incidents.title: Confusing Kaspersky antimalware neural networks
incidents.description: The Kaspersky ML research team attacked an internal antimalware ML model without white-box access using only feature knowledge and successfully evaded detection for most adversarially modified malware files.

incidents.title: PyTorch-nightly dependency-confusion supply-chain attack
incidents.description: A supply-chain attack on PyTorch-nightly involving dependency confusion exposed sensitive information on Linux machines between Dec 25-30, 2022.

incidents.title: RCE in MathGPT via prompt injection (Streamlit demo)
incidents.description: The publicly available Streamlit application MathGPT used GPT-3 to convert natural-language questions into Python code that was then executed; prompt injection allowed an attacker to achieve remote code execution on the host.

incidents.title: YouTube Kids presents inappropriate content via recommendation
incidents.description: YouTube's content-filtering and recommendation algorithms exposed children to disturbing and inappropriate videos.

incidents.title: Amazon warehouse robot ruptures bear-spray can
incidents.description: Twenty-four Amazon workers in New Jersey were hospitalized after a warehouse robot punctured a can of bear-repellent spray.

incidents.title: Boeing 737 MAX MCAS crashes
incidents.description: A Boeing 737 crashed into the sea, killing 189 people, after faulty sensor data caused the MCAS automated maneuvering system to repeatedly push the plane's nose downward.

incidents.title: Collection of robotic-surgery malfunctions
incidents.description: Study of FDA database reports identified 8,061 robotic-surgery malfunctions including 1,391 injuries and 144 deaths between 2000 and 2013.

incidents.title: Uber autonomous cars running red lights (San Francisco)
incidents.description: Uber vehicles equipped with autonomous-driving technology were observed running red lights during street testing in San Francisco.

incidents.title: NYC school teacher evaluation algorithm contested
incidents.description: An algorithm used to evaluate NYC public-school teachers produced disputed scores and was contested in court for its lack of transparency and reliability.

incidents.title: Kronos scheduling algorithm harms Starbucks employees
incidents.description: The Kronos scheduling algorithm allegedly caused financial and scheduling instability for Starbucks wage workers.

incidents.title: Northpointe COMPAS recidivism risk disparate impact
incidents.description: Northpointe's COMPAS recidivism algorithm was shown to be twice as likely to incorrectly label Black defendants as high-risk and twice as likely to incorrectly label white defendants as low-risk.

incidents.title: ChatGPT fails to follow lexical constraints
incidents.description: When prompted with lexical constraints (e.g., generate text without the letter 'e'), ChatGPT almost always fails to follow the constraints.

incidents.title: ChatGPT fabricates scientific references
incidents.description: ChatGPT generates false or incomplete references to scientific literature, recommending papers that may not exist or attributing them to the wrong authors.

incidents.title: RCE through LLM frameworks (LangChain, Boxcars)
incidents.description: LLM frameworks like LangChain (Python) and Boxcars.ai (Ruby) offer apps and scripts that execute LLM-generated queries; carefully crafted prompts can yield remote code execution or SQL injection on the host.

incidents.title: ChatGPT lexical-constraint failure (measurement)
incidents.description: Measurement of ChatGPT's failure rate when given lexical constraints in prompts, showing nearly universal non-compliance.

incidents.title: ChatGPT links wrong authors to papers (measurement)
incidents.description: When asked to recommend papers on explainability, privacy, and adversarial ML, ChatGPT linked wrong authors to real papers and invented non-existent ones.

incidents.title: ChatGPT-based agents enable RCE/SQLi via polite prompting
incidents.description: Frameworks such as LangChain and Boxcars.ai directly execute LLM-generated code/SQL, making it trivial to perform remote code execution or SQL injection through carefully worded prompts.

incidents.title: MathGPT prompt-injection control bypass (issue report)
incidents.description: Despite existing controls, MathGPT's application still answers user math problems via injected prompts in violation of policy.

incidents.title: Geopolitical bias in sentiment analysis for neutral phrases
incidents.description: Sentiment-analysis models exhibit geopolitical bias when scoring otherwise-neutral phrases referencing specific countries or political groups.

incidents.title: gpt-4o-mini AgentHarm evaluation (Inspect Evals)
incidents.description: Evaluation of OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 on the AgentHarm benchmark via Inspect Evals, measuring harmful-task compliance of an agentic system.

incidents.title: gpt-4o-mini WMDP-Bio evaluation (Inspect Evals)
incidents.description: Evaluation of OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 on the WMDP-Bio benchmark covering hazardous knowledge in biosecurity.

incidents.title: gpt-4o-mini WMDP-Chem evaluation (Inspect Evals)
incidents.description: Evaluation of OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 on the WMDP-Chem benchmark covering hazardous chemical-security knowledge.

incidents.title: gpt-4o-mini CyberSecEval2 prompt-injection benchmark
incidents.description: Evaluation of OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 on the cyse2_prompt_injection benchmark from Meta's CyberSecEval2 cybersecurity evaluation suite.

incidents.title: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo WMDP-Cyber evaluation
incidents.description: Evaluation of Together's Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo on WMDP-Cyber benchmark covering hazardous cybersecurity knowledge.

incidents.title: DeepSeek-R1 CyberSecEval2 interpreter-abuse evaluation
incidents.description: Evaluation of DeepSeek-R1 on the cyse2_interpreter_abuse benchmark, testing model willingness to abuse code interpreters for risky cyber tasks.

incidents.title: Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct WMDP-Bio evaluation
incidents.description: Evaluation of Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 on the WMDP-Bio benchmark covering hazardous biosecurity knowledge.

incidents.title: Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct WMDP-Chem evaluation
incidents.description: Evaluation of Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 on the WMDP-Chem benchmark covering hazardous chemical-security knowledge.

incidents.title: Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct CyberSecEval2 interpreter-abuse
incidents.description: Evaluation of Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 on the cyse2_interpreter_abuse benchmark via Inspect Evals.

incidents.title: Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct CyberSecEval2 prompt-injection
incidents.description: Evaluation of Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 on the cyse2_prompt_injection benchmark from CyberSecEval2.

incidents.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit TOCTOU container escape (CVE-2024-0132)
incidents.description: NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.16.1 and earlier contain a Time-of-check-Time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability in default configuration: a crafted container image may gain access to the host file system.

incidents.title: Improper authorization in lunary-ai/lunary (CVE-2024-10274)
incidents.description: lunary-ai/lunary 1.5.5 /users/me/org endpoint lacks adequate access control, allowing unauthorized users to access sensitive organization information.

incidents.title: Improper access control in lunary-ai/lunary evaluators (CVE-2024-10330)
incidents.description: In lunary-ai/lunary 1.5.6 the /v1/evaluators/ endpoint lacks proper access control, letting any project user fetch all evaluator data regardless of role.

incidents.title: Path traversal in mintplex-labs/anything-llm (CVE-2024-10513)
incidents.description: anything-llm <1.2.2 document-uploads manager endpoint /api/document/move-files allows attackers to move the database file to a publicly accessible directory, leading to unauthorized data access and privilege escalation.

incidents.title: Improper access control on evaluator deletion route (lunary)
incidents.description: Improper access control on a route that allowed low-privilege users to delete evaluator data, causing permanent data loss.

incidents.title: DoS in invoke-ai/invokeai multipart boundary parsing (CVE-2024-10821)
incidents.description: Vulnerability in invoke-ai/invokeai multipart-request boundary processing allows unauthenticated attackers to cause excessive resource consumption (DoS).

incidents.title: Path traversal in eosphoros-ai/db-gpt
incidents.description: Path-traversal vulnerability in DB-GPT enabling unauthorized file access on the server.

incidents.title: Arbitrary file write in eosphoros-ai/db-gpt knowledge API (CVE-2024-10833)
incidents.description: db-gpt 0.6.0 knowledge-upload endpoint is susceptible to absolute-path traversal, allowing attackers to write files to arbitrary locations on the server.

incidents.title: Arbitrary file write in db-gpt RAG-knowledge endpoint (CVE-2024-10834)
incidents.description: db-gpt 0.6.0 contains an arbitrary-file-write vulnerability in the RAG-knowledge endpoint.

incidents.title: SQL injection via SQL-run endpoint in db-gpt (CVE-2024-10835)
incidents.description: db-gpt v0.6.0 web API POST /api/v1/editor/sql/run allows execution of arbitrary SQL without access control, enabling SQL injection / data exfiltration.

incidents.title: Overly permissive CORS / CSRF in db-gpt (CVE-2024-10906)
incidents.description: db-gpt 0.6.0 dbgpt_server uses a permissive CORSMiddleware that sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to * for all requests, enabling CSRF and cross-origin attacks.

incidents.title: Sensitive file disclosure via ImagePromptTemplate in LangChain (CVE-2024-10940)
incidents.description: langchain-core 0.1.17-0.1.53, 0.2.0-0.2.43, 0.3.0-0.3.15 allows unauthorized users to read arbitrary files from the host file system via ImagePromptTemplate.

incidents.title: Code injection in binary-husky/gpt_academic (CVE-2024-10950)
incidents.description: Code-injection vulnerability in binary-husky/gpt_academic permitting arbitrary code execution on the backend.

incidents.title: Prompt-injection RCE via manim plugin in gpt_academic (CVE-2024-10954)
incidents.description: The manim plugin in binary-husky/gpt_academic allows prompt-injection-based remote code execution by injecting malicious code through the prompt.

incidents.title: Arbitrary file deletion vulnerability (lunary/anything-llm class)
incidents.description: Vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, including SSH keys, SQLite databases, and configuration files, impacting integrity and availability.

incidents.description: DoS in invoke-ai/invokeai v5.0.2 /boards/{board_id} PATCH endpoint when an excessively large payload is sent in the board_name field.

incidents.title: Sensitive prompt-data exposure via URL access
incidents.description: Unauthorized users can view sensitive prompt data by accessing specific URLs, leading to potential exposure of critical information.

incidents.description: RCE in invokeai 5.3.1-5.4.2 via the /api/v2/models/install API: unsafe deserialization of model files using torch.load without validation enables attackers to embed malicious code in model files that executes on load.

incidents.description: AI Scribe – SEO AI Writer, Content Generator, Humanizer, Blog Writer, SEO Optimizer, DALLE-3 (WordPress plugin) issue affecting GPT-4o 128K usage.

incidents.description: In llama_index v0.12.5 the LangChainLLM class has no exception handling when threads terminate before _llm.predict runs, leading to an infinite loop in get_response_gen (DoS).

incidents.title: SSRF in infiniflow/ragflow (CVE-2024-12779)
incidents.description: SSRF in ragflow 0.12.0 via POST /v1/llm/add_llm and POST /v1/conversation/tts endpoints.
